title: Al-Assisted Early Detection System for Osteoarthritis (OA) Risk Markers in North Eastern Region (NER)
org: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
department: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
description:
Background:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most common musculoskeletal disorders affecting elderly individuals and physically active populations, leading to chronic pain, joint stiffness, mobility issues, and reduced quality of life.
In the North Eastern Region (NER), difficult terrain, physically demanding livelihoods, aging population, and limited access to specialized orthopaedic care further increase the burden of undiagnosed and untreated osteoarthritis cases. Early identification of OA risk markers is critical for timely intervention and preventive healthcare management.
However, healthcare facilities in many remote and rural areas of NER lack affordable screening tools, specialist support, and diagnostic infrastructure for early-stage detection of osteoarthritis. There is a need for a technology-driven solution that can assist healthcare workers in identifying early OA indicators and supporting preventive screening in low-resource settings across the North Eastern Region.
Description:
This problem statement seeks to develop an AI-assisted screening and detection system for identifying early risk markers and symptoms associated with Osteoarthritis (OA) in the North Eastern Region. The solution should:
a. Assist in early detection of OA-related risk markers through
• Joint movement analysis
• Gait and posture assessment
• Pain and mobility screening inputs
• Medical imaging or sensor-based assessment (if applicable)
b. Use AI/ML techniques to analyse patient data and identify high-risk cases for early intervention c. Support screening in primary healthcare centres, rural health camps, and community outreach programs d. Provide preliminary OA risk assessment and severity indication e. Enable healthcare workers to digitally record patient symptoms and screening reports f. Include multilingual and easy-to-use interfaces suitable for rural healthcare settings in NER g. Work in low-connectivity environments with offline data collection capability h. Provide awareness and preventive guidance related to joint care, physical activity, nutrition, and lifestyle management The solution should be portable, affordable, and suitable for deployment in remote and underserved areas.
Expected Solution:
A scalable Al-enabled healthcare screening solution with:
• Al-based OA risk analysis and screening module
• Portable assessment interface or sensor-assisted screening mechanism
• Digital patient record and report generation system
• Mobile/web-based healthcare worker interface
• Offline synchronization capability for remote areas
• Multilingual support and simplified workflow for field deployment
• Secure patient data management and analytics dashboard The solution should support early diagnosis, preventive healthcare intervention, and improved accessibility to musculoskeletal healthcare services in the North Eastern Region.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, ml applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (2/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Space Technology. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on sensor, infrastructure. Sustainability (2/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Assisted Early Detection System for Osteoarthritis (OA) Risk Markers in North Eastern Region (NER)

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a tool that helps health workers in remote NER clinics spot early signs of osteoarthritis, using gait, movement, and basic screening inputs, without needing a specialist on site.
overview.why_it_matters: Physically demanding rural livelihoods plus zero specialist access means OA often goes undiagnosed until it's disabling. Early flagging changes that trajectory for real people.
pain_points: No affordable screening tools available in remote NER healthcare facilities.
Specialist orthopaedic support is essentially absent in rural areas.
Undiagnosed cases progress untreated until mobility is seriously affected.
overview.background: OA burden is elevated in NER due to physically demanding livelihoods and an aging population, but diagnostic infrastructure for early detection doesn't reach rural areas.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-assisted screening system using joint movement analysis, gait/posture assessment, and mobility screening inputs to flag early OA risk markers for frontline health workers.
expected_solution: Movement/gait analysis for OA risk indicators.
Screening workflow usable by non-specialist health workers.
Support for basic medical imaging input where available.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate-High. Gait/movement-based screening using computer vision is an established research area, applying it to a low-resource frontline-worker context is the real innovation angle.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High, but flagged Hardware category, likely because it may need a camera/sensor rig for gait capture, that's a meaningfully harder build than pure software.

competitive_landscape.note: Movement-analysis health screening is a recurring hackathon category; differentiate by building specifically for a non-specialist operator, not a clinical-grade tool.

innovation.note: Applying gait/movement AI to frontline non-specialist screening, rather than clinical diagnosis, is the differentiator.

invention.note: Movement capture plus AI analysis plus a usable screening workflow is a genuinely full-stack build.

technical_feasibility.note: Hardware category plus AI analysis in 36 hours is ambitious, a smartphone-camera-based capture is far more feasible than dedicated sensor hardware.

impact_and_benefits.note: Early OA flagging in a population with zero specialist access has clear, real preventive-care value.

architecture.note: Capture device/camera, movement analysis model, and a simple frontline workflow, three pieces but not deeply interdependent.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow, real value but the Hardware framing plus AI analysis stacks meaningful feasibility risk in 36 hours. Going smartphone-camera-only rather than dedicated hardware materially de-risks it.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Clear underserved-population need with a concrete, testable use case: a health worker screens a patient in minutes.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: If the team commits to custom sensor hardware instead of a smartphone camera, the build likely won't reach a working state in time.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Decide immediately: smartphone-camera-based gait capture (feasible) or dedicated wearable sensors (much harder), this single choice determines whether the PS is buildable in 36 hours.

idea_0_4: Commit to smartphone-camera-based capture over custom hardware, this is the single highest-leverage scope decision.
Define the specific gait/movement markers you'll analyze, don't try to cover joint analysis, gait, posture, and imaging all at once.
Assign one person to capture/data pipeline, one to the analysis model.
prototype_4_22: Build the video capture and basic pose-estimation pipeline (open pose-estimation libraries exist and are usable off the shelf).
Build the risk-scoring logic from movement features.
Design the health-worker-facing screening flow, simple, guided, non-technical.
integration_22_30: Connect capture -> analysis -> risk flag -> referral guidance end to end.
Test with varied movement samples, not just one clean walk.
Handle low-light/poor-camera-quality gracefully, this is a real rural-clinic constraint.
polish_30_36: Finalize the screening workflow UI for a non-specialist operator.
Rehearse a live screening demo, capture, analyze, flag, in front of judges.
Prepare your answer for how this compares to and supports, not replaces, an actual orthopaedic diagnosis.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Run a live gait capture and screening on a volunteer during the demo, a working real-time flag is far more convincing than a slide of accuracy numbers.

strengths: Concrete, demoable use case, a health worker screening a real patient.
weaknesses: Hardware framing plus AI in 36 hours is genuinely tight, scope discipline is essential.
Risk of over-promising clinical-grade accuracy that a real screening tool can't deliver.

roles_needed: UX person for the frontline-worker flow
team_fit.ideal_ratio: 1-2 CV-focused, 1 UX-focused, 1 doing OA-domain research so the risk logic isn't guessed.
team_fit.approach: Get one person researching actual OA risk indicators from movement (real clinical literature) while the pipeline is built in parallel.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Pose-estimation integration using existing libraries, and the screening-flow UI shell.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Which movement features actually correlate with OA risk, this needs real domain research, not assumed correlations.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A model flagging 'risk' based on made-up feature weights rather than real clinical indicators could give false reassurance or false alarm, both are harmful in a health context.

data_resource_availability.status: No public gait/OA dataset is trivially available; this is a genuine data gap.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Use your own team's movement as sample/test data (clearly labeled as non-clinical demo data), and cite real published OA risk-marker research to justify your feature choices even without a full training dataset.

judge_qna.question: What clinical evidence backs the movement markers you're screening for?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific research your risk markers are based on, don't present them as self-evident, judges will ask what grounds the model.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would you validate this against actual diagnosed OA cases?

judge_qna.question: Could this tool give a false negative that delays real diagnosis?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Frame it explicitly as a screening/referral trigger, not a diagnosis, every flagged case should be routed to a real clinical follow-up, never treated as final.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your threshold for flagging, and how conservative is it?
